data_leaves_device: Nothing leaves the cuff except over BLE to the connected phone; what the vendor app then uploaded (readings, account identity) is the app's business and the service is gone.
cloud.failure_mode: Already happened. Qardio's servers became intermittent from 2025-03-12 and went down for good on the morning of 2025-04-29 (Apple Support Community thread 256006237, replies dated 2025-04-30 and 2025-05-04). The vendor app could no longer sign in or sync, and since the app would not show its START button without a signed-in account, the cuff became unusable through the official software. Nothing on the device itself changed: the BLE control surface above is complete and local, which is why LibreArm (2025-09) could revive it with no cloud at all. The iOS app disappeared from the App Store around 2024-09-21 and briefly returned; by 2026 both store listings were gone and the vendor's domain had been seen listed for sale.
cloud.notes: Recorded only to document the dependency that killed the official app. There is no cloud interface to implement and no reason to.
cloud.vendor_service: Qardio cloud (account, measurement history, sharing) — offline since 2025-04-29

methods.notes: Both open clients scan on the advertised 0x1810 service alone and use no name filter, so the service match is the one that is known to work. 0x1810 is shared with every SIG-profile blood pressure monitor (Beurer, Omron and others in this catalogue), so the name narrows it: the vendor manual's phone screenshots list the bonded cuff as "QardioARM" / "QardioArm" (the manual itself spells it both ways, hence the prefix match). A connected client can confirm the model definitively by the presence of the vendor control characteristic 583cb5b3-875d-40ed-9098-c39eb0c1983d. The cuff advertises only while switched on, which means unwrapped from the pump unit; wrapped, or after a few idle minutes, it is off and invisible.

device.manufacturer: Qardio, Inc. (San Francisco); built by Ya Horng Electronic, Taiwan
device.name: QardioArm (A100) Wireless Blood Pressure Monitor
device.notes:
An upper-arm oscillometric blood-pressure cuff that folds around its own pump unit and runs on four AAA cells. It has no screen and no button: unwrapping the cuff switches it on, wrapping it back switches it off, and every measurement is started from a phone over BLE. That made it entirely dependent on the vendor app, and the vendor is gone — the app left the stores and the Qardio cloud it synced to went dark in 2025.
The protocol turns out to be almost entirely standard. The cuff implements the Bluetooth SIG Blood Pressure Service (0x1810) and delivers results as Blood Pressure Measurement (0x2a35) records, so any client that decodes IEEE-11073 SFLOATs can read it. The one vendor addition is a control characteristic inside the same service that takes a two-byte command: f1 01 inflates and measures, f1 02 cancels. The cuff bonds to the phone, and the only "reset" it has is a pinhole on the battery hatch that clears that bond.
Partial records arrive while the cuff inflates and deflates; a client must treat a reading as a result only when systolic and diastolic are both finite, positive and systolic exceeds diastolic (the completeness rule both open clients apply). Readings are a wellness log, not a clinical instrument — see safety_advisory.

openness.notes: Qardio published nothing about the control characteristic. Everything vendor-specific here was recovered by the LibreArm author from the cuff's behaviour; the measurement format itself is the Bluetooth SIG's published Blood Pressure Measurement characteristic.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: The cuff is pairable whenever it is switched on, which is whenever it is unwrapped; there is no pairing button. The manual's "touch your phone to the QardioArm" is proximity theatre for the first connection — the cuff has no NFC and the bond is established over BLE when the app first subscribes.

exclusivity.recovery: Forget the QardioArm in the phone's Bluetooth settings, press the pinhole on the battery hatch with a paper clip while the cuff is unwrapped (green light through the hatch), then connect again and accept the pairing prompt. Close the vendor app, if one is still installed, before connecting.

pairing.notes: Established from behaviour, not a capture: the vendor manual tells the user to accept a pairing request with no code to type, the paired cuff appears in the phone's Bluetooth device list, and LibreArm maps ATT errors 0x05 (insufficient authentication), 0x08 (insufficient authorization), 0x0c (insufficient encryption key size) and 0x0f (insufficient encryption) on its notification enable or start write to "the cuff needs re-pairing". That pattern is a secured characteristic behind a Just Works bond. The Android port never calls for a bond itself and still works, which is consistent with the stack bonding on demand when the cuff returns one of those errors. Whether the cuff uses LE legacy pairing or LE Secure Connections is not established.

unpair.clears: The stored bond only. The cuff holds no readings, name or settings.
unpair.notes: The pinhole press under factory_reset is this operation; the cuff has nothing else to reset, so the two are one procedure. Forget the device on the phone as well, or the phone reconnects with keys the cuff no longer has and the cuff refuses it.

safety_advisory.detail: Starting a measurement pumps the cuff up on whoever is wearing it. Only start one when the cuff is fitted to a consenting adult who is sitting still, with the arm supported at heart level, and stay with them until it deflates; use cancel (f1 02) if it must stop early. The manual's cuff range is 22-37 cm upper-arm circumference, and it advises consulting a doctor before use in pregnancy, arrhythmia or arteriosclerosis. Readings taken through a third-party client are a personal log: they are not diagnostic, and a reading must never be the sole basis for a medication decision. A client must display the values the cuff reports without altering them, and should show the irregular-pulse flag when the record carries it. This spec and any client built from it are experimental and unaffiliated with Qardio; the manufacturer's instructions for use govern.
safety_advisory.summary: The cuff inflates around the arm when a measurement is started, and its readings are not a substitute for clinical blood-pressure measurement or medical advice.

credentials.notes: No application-layer secret, PIN or account token. The bond is the only credential, and it lives in the OS Bluetooth stack on both sides.
stored_on_device: One BLE bond (long-term key) for the paired central

factory_reset.description: The vendor manual calls this "resetting the pairing" and it is the remedy both for moving the cuff to a new phone and for a phone that has forgotten a bond the cuff still holds. LibreArm's own recovery advice on a pairing-class ATT error is the same three moves: press the pinhole, forget the cuff in the phone's Bluetooth settings, reconnect. The button sits behind a pinhole on the battery compartment hatch and needs a straightened paper clip. The cuff must be switched on (unwrapped) for the press to register.
factory_reset.effect: Clears the stored BLE bond ("the pairing"). The manual documents nothing else held on the cuff, so this is the only reset it has.

procedures.basis: QardioArm user manual v2.4, "Resetting the pairing" (page 15); LibreArm's pairing-error recovery text; the MedM support page for the QardioArm, which describes the same press and the same green light.
procedures.indicator: A green light shines through the battery compartment hatch.
procedures.name: Paper clip in the battery-hatch pinhole

steps.action: Unwrap the cuff from the pump unit so the cuff is switched on.
Press the button behind the pinhole on the battery compartment hatch with a straightened paper clip.
steps.expect: A green light shines through the hatch; the stored bond is gone.

steps.action: On the phone that was paired, open Bluetooth settings and forget the QardioArm entry so the phone does not try to reuse the old keys.
Connect and enable notifications on 00002a35-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb; accept the new pairing prompt.

methods.description: The whole flow as LibreArm runs it. The cuff is switched on by unwrapping it, bonds on the first secured operation, streams 0x2a35 records once notifications are enabled, and measures when f1 01 is written to the control characteristic.
methods.name: Unwrap, bond, subscribe, start

steps.action: Fit four AAA alkaline cells if the cuff is new or dead, and unwrap the cuff from the pump unit to switch it on.
steps.expect: The cuff starts advertising service 0x1810 within a few seconds.

steps.action: Scan for an advertisement carrying service 00001810-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and connect.

steps.expect: One byte, 0-100 percent. LibreArm refuses to start below 10 percent and warns below 20.

On a fresh cuff the OS raises a pairing prompt here; accept it. An ATT error 0x05, 0x08, 0x0c or 0x0f instead means the cuff holds a bond for another phone — clear it with the pinhole (see factory_reset) and retry.

steps.action: Fit the cuff on the upper arm, Qardio logo towards the hand, arm supported at heart level.
Write f1 01 to 583cb5b3-875d-40ed-9098-c39eb0c1983d to start the measurement.
steps.expect: The cuff inflates. 0x2a35 notifications follow while it inflates and deflates; keep the one whose systolic and diastolic are both finite and positive with systolic above diastolic. LibreArm abandons a run that produces none within 180 s.

steps.action: Wrap the cuff back around the pump unit when done to switch the cuff off.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision — no account, no network, no cloud. A new or second-hand cuff needs only batteries and a phone that can bond to it. The vendor app once required a Qardio account before it would show the START button; that was an app-side gate, not a device one, and both open clients drive the cuff without any account. The one thing that stops a connect-and-go client is a bond the cuff still holds for an earlier phone, which the pinhole clears.

rejoin.notes: BLE-only; there is no network to rejoin. Moving the cuff to a new phone means clearing the bond with the pinhole and forgetting it on the old phone — the pairing reset above, which is not a loss of anything else because the cuff stores nothing else.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Every byte here is read from two open-source clients that are used daily against real cuffs (LibreArm on iOS, its Android port), cross-checked against the vendor app's string table and the Bluetooth SIG characteristic definition. The worked payload examples in payload_formats are constructed from the SIG layout, not captured from a cuff; no raw QardioArm frame has been published.

entities.name: Systolic Pressure
entities.notes: SFLOAT decode required; publish only from a complete record (see payload_formats.BloodPressureMeasurement). Shown in mmHg; convert if the record's flags bit 0 says kPa.

entities.name: Diastolic Pressure
entities.notes: Same decode and completeness rule as Systolic Pressure.

entities.name: Mean Arterial Pressure
entities.notes: Same decode as Systolic Pressure; may be a special value (no reading) on a record that carries the other two.

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: Read, not notified; absent on a cuff that does not expose the Battery Service.

entities.name: Start Measurement
entities.notes: Inflates the cuff on whoever is wearing it; the safety_advisory banner applies to this control above all. Pulse arrives in the same 0x2a35 record as the pressures but at a flag-dependent offset, so it is documented in payload_formats rather than bound as an entity.

artifacts.description: MIT-licensed iOS client in daily use against real cuffs. Source of the control characteristic UUID, the f1 01 / f1 02 bytes, the notify-on-0x2a35 flow, the battery handling, the pairing-class ATT error list and recovery advice, the SFLOAT decode with its special values, the kPa factor, and the completeness and save-range rules. Scans on service 0x1810 only; no name filter. Facts only were taken; no code was transcribed.

MIT-licensed Android port by Drew Green. Independently confirms the same service, characteristic and control UUIDs and the same two command bytes; writes CCCD 01 00 (notifications) on 0x2a35 and receives records; writes the control characteristic with response. It never requests a bond itself and does no kPa or special-value handling — recorded here as a weaker parser, not as a protocol fact.

The LibreArm author's write-up (2025-09-28): the cuff speaks the standard SIG Blood Pressure Measurement service, a vendor characteristic controls inflation, partial values arrive while inflating, and the app saves only records with systolic and diastolic present.

artifacts.artifact: QardioArm user manual, version 2.4, English (Qardio, Inc. 2013-2014)
artifacts.description: Unwrap-to-power-on and wrap-to-power-off behaviour, auto power-off, the first-use pairing flow ("accept the pairing request"), the "Resetting the pairing" pinhole procedure and green-light indicator, battery type and low-battery behaviour, measurement ranges, FCC/IC identifiers and the OEM.

Public mirror of the Bluetooth SIG Blood Pressure Measurement characteristic definition: field order, flags bits, measurement status bits and the C1-C6 presence conditions used for the format and payload_formats blocks.

artifacts.artifact: com.getqardio.android 2.5.1 (vendor Android app, delisted; third-party mirror, 2026-08-03)
artifacts.description: String-table triage only, no decompiled code read. Confirms the 0x1810 / 0x2a35 pair and the 583cb5b3 control UUID, and shows the Nordic legacy DFU UUID set plus part of the Secure DFU family — the basis for the hedged firmware_update feature. The same app served the QardioBase scale and QardioCore patch, so nothing in it is attributable to the cuff alone.

Apple Support Community thread opened 2025-03-13 reporting the Qardio servers down; replies dated 2025-04-30 and 2025-05-04 date the permanent outage to the morning of 2025-04-29. Thread 255768352 (2024-09-21) records the iOS app vanishing from the App Store and returning within days.

2026-05-19 post-mortem: no shutdown announcement, UK and Dutch corporate filings (Qardio Netherlands B.V. bankruptcy at its own request after funding from Qardio, Inc. stopped), apps gone from the stores, the vendor domain seen listed for sale, and the cuff unusable without its app — with LibreArm named as the way out.

evidence.documentation_review: Two independent open-source clients, the vendor manual and the SIG characteristic definition were read on 2026-10-11 and agree on every fact declared above. The two clients share an author lineage (the Android port is a deliberate mirror of the iOS client), so they count as one recovery confirmed twice, not two recoveries. The vendor app's string table was used only to confirm UUIDs and to note the DFU library.
evidence.open_questions: Which flags the cuff actually sets in its 0x2a35 records (timestamp? user ID? status?), and therefore where pulse sits; whether the characteristic is declared notify, indicate or both; whether the control characteristic is write, write-without-response or both; the exact ATT error the cuff returns on an unbonded notification enable; whether the Battery Service is present on every hardware revision; whether any DFU service appears in the cuff's own GATT table; and the advertised local name, which rests on the manual's phone screenshots.

dfu_mode.notes: Not observed. A stock legacy bootloader advertises "DfuTarg" and may or may not move address; nothing yet binds such an advert back to a QardioArm.

enter.notes: Nothing here says the cuff honours the stack's buttonless entry (01 04 on the legacy control point) or carries the DFU service at all in application mode — see dfu.notes. No entry command is declared.

image.notes: The vendor Android app's string table carries the complete Nordic legacy DFU UUID set (service 00001530-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 and its 1531/1532/1534 characteristics) and part of the Secure DFU 8ec9... family, i.e. it bundles Nordic's DFU client library. Where it fetched images from, and whether it ever updated the cuff rather than a sibling product, is not established.

dfu.notes: Declared to the extent the sources establish it and no further. The evidence is the DFU library inside a vendor app that served the QardioArm, the QardioBase scale and the QardioCore ECG patch alike; neither open client discovers a DFU service on the cuff (they only look for 0x1810 and 0x180f), and no GATT dump has been published. So: the cuff's radio is very likely a Nordic nRF5 part and the app could flash Nordic devices, but which Qardio product that applied to is unknown. A GATT explorer should treat 00001530-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 as read-only if it appears. With the vendor gone no new image will ever ship; the only use of this block is recognising a cuff stranded in its bootloader.

covers: Starting and cancelling a measurement (vendor control characteristic)
Systolic, diastolic, mean arterial pressure and pulse from the standard 0x2a35 record, including the irregular-pulse status bit when present
Battery level via the standard Battery Service, where exposed
not_covered: Measurement history: the cuff stores none, so a client keeps its own (LibreArm writes to Apple Health / Google Fit)
Firmware updates: the vendor's images, if any, are gone with the vendor
local_access.notes: No bridge, no hub, no replacement part. The only thing a user needs that they no longer have is a client, and two exist.
local_access.summary: Fully local as shipped: the cuff speaks the SIG Blood Pressure Service over BLE plus one two-byte vendor command, with no account, token or server at any point. Two open-source clients prove it daily.

BloodPressureMeasurement.description: One 0x2a35 notification. Offsets 0-6 are fixed and declared in the characteristic's format block; this entry gives the walk over the optional tail and the SFLOAT rule, with worked examples that scripts/test_qardio_arm_spec.py decodes. The examples are constructed from the SIG layout to exercise a decoder — no raw QardioArm frame has been published — so they show what a conformant record looks like, not which flags the cuff sets.

fields.description: Byte 0. bit0 unit (0 mmHg, 1 kPa); bit1 timestamp; bit2 pulse; bit3 user ID; bit4 measurement status; bits 5-7 reserved.
fields.name: flags

fields.description: 7 bytes at offset 7 when flags bit1 is set: year uint16 LE, month, day, hour, minute, second. Neither open client uses it.
fields.name: timestamp

fields.description: SFLOAT LE, 2 bytes, after the timestamp (or at offset 7 without one) when flags bit2 is set.
fields.name: pulse_rate

fields.description: uint8 after the pulse rate when flags bit3 is set; 255 = unknown user.
fields.name: user_id

fields.description: uint16 LE at the end when flags bit4 is set. bit0 body movement; bit1 cuff too loose; bit2 irregular pulse detected (the one bit LibreArm surfaces); bits 3-4 pulse-rate range (0 in range, 1 above upper limit, 2 below lower limit); bit5 improper measurement position; bits 6-15 reserved.
fields.name: measurement_status

parse_rules: Require at least 7 bytes. Read flags at byte 0; if any of bits 5-7 is set, reject the record.

Decode systolic (1-2), diastolic (3-4) and MAP (5-6) as little-endian SFLOATs: mantissa = low 12 bits as two's complement (subtract 0x1000 when >= 0x800), exponent = high 4 bits as two's complement (subtract 16 when >= 8), value = mantissa x 10^exponent.
Mantissa 0x07ff is NaN, 0x0800 NRes, 0x07fe +INF, 0x0802 -INF, 0x0801 reserved: no value, whatever the exponent.
If flags bit0 is set the three pressures are kPa; multiply by 7.500617 for mmHg.

Walk the tail from offset 7 in flag order: bit1 -> skip or decode 7 timestamp bytes; bit2 -> 2-byte SFLOAT pulse in bpm; bit3 -> 1 byte user ID; bit4 -> 2-byte LE status. Each must fit, and the walk must end exactly at the record's length.
A record is a result only when systolic and diastolic are both finite and > 0 and systolic > diastolic; anything else is an in-progress frame or a failed measurement and is not shown as a reading.
Worked: 04 78 00 50 00 5f 00 48 00 = mmHg, pulse present: systolic 120, diastolic 80, MAP 95, pulse 72.
Worked (kPa): 05 a0 f0 6a f0 7f f0 48 00 = kPa, pulse present: 16.0 / 10.6 / 12.7 kPa (SFLOAT 0xf0a0 = 160 x 10^-1), i.e. 120.0 / 79.5 / 95.3 mmHg; pulse 72.
Worked (all fields): 1e 78 00 50 00 5f 00 e9 07 0a 0b 08 1e 00 48 00 ff 04 00 = timestamp 2025-10-11 08:30:00, pulse 72, user 255, status 0x0004 (irregular pulse).
Worked (no result yet): 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 = flags 0, all pressures zero; and 04 ff 07 ff 07 ff 07 48 00 = NaN pressures. Neither is a reading.

control_commands.notes: Only these two opcodes are known. The first byte f1 may be a command class with other opcodes behind it; nobody has probed, and probing a medical device's control characteristic blind is not recommended.

hardware.batteries: 4 x AAA alkaline (the manual excludes rechargeables)
hardware.measurement_range: 40-250 mmHg pressure; 40-200 bpm pulse; 1 mmHg / 1 bpm resolution (manual)
hardware.oem: Ya Horng Electronic Co., Ltd., Tainan, Taiwan

measurement_session.multi_run_delay_s: 15-60 (default 30) between readings when averaging up to three
measurement_session.notes: LibreArm's values, recorded as a known-good envelope rather than protocol constants. The cuff itself imposes none of them except that it switches off after a few idle minutes when left unwrapped.

pairing_error_codes.notes: ATT insufficient authentication, insufficient authorization, insufficient encryption key size and insufficient encryption, returned on the 0x2a35 notification enable or the f1 01 write. All four mean the same thing operationally: the bond on one side does not match the other. Remedy under device.pairing.exclusivity.recovery.

protocol_details.power_behaviour: No power button. Unwrapping the cuff from the pump unit switches the cuff on and starts advertising; wrapping it back switches it off; left unwrapped and idle it switches off by itself after a few minutes (vendor manual, page 9). A client that cannot find the cuff should tell the user to unwrap it, not to press anything.

remaining_unknowns: No raw 0x2a35 record from a QardioArm has been published, so which optional fields the cuff includes is unknown. Pulse rate is therefore documented in payload_formats with its flag-dependent offset and has no sensor entity; one captured record would let it be bound at a fixed offset.

The advertised local name. The manual's screenshots show the bonded cuff as QardioARM / QardioArm in the phone's Bluetooth list; neither open client filters on a name. The prefix matcher 'Qardio' rests on that.

Whether the cuff exposes Blood Pressure Feature (0x2a49), Intermediate Cuff Pressure (0x2a36), Device Information (0x180a) or any DFU service: no GATT dump has been published and the open clients discover only 0x1810 and 0x180f.

What an in-progress (inflating) record carries in its pressure fields — zeros, special values or rising partial values. The clients only establish that such records exist and fail the completeness rule.
The pairing method in detail: Just Works is inferred from a code-free prompt and the ATT error pattern, not from a capture. LE legacy vs LE Secure Connections is unknown.
Whether the f1 command byte has opcodes beyond 01 and 02. Not probed, deliberately.
Whether the pinhole clears anything beyond the bond. The manual documents nothing else stored on the cuff.
The hardware variant map. The manual is for the original QardioArm (FCC ID 2ABF2-888ARM; FDA K140067 names model A100); whether later colour variants or an A101 differ in firmware is unknown.

format.name: flags_unit_kpa
format.notes: Flags bit 0: the unit of the three pressure SFLOATs.

format.name: flags_timestamp_present
format.notes: Flags bit 1: a 7-byte timestamp (year uint16 LE, month, day, hour, minute, second) follows at offset 7.

format.name: flags_pulse_present
format.notes: Flags bit 2: a pulse-rate SFLOAT follows the timestamp (or sits at offset 7 when there is none).

format.name: flags_user_id_present
format.notes: Flags bit 3: a uint8 user ID follows the pulse rate; 255 = unknown user.

format.name: flags_status_present
format.notes: Flags bit 4: a uint16 LE measurement-status bitfield ends the record. Bits 5-7 are reserved and LibreArm rejects a record with any of them set.

format.name: systolic_sfloat
format.notes: IEEE-11073 SFLOAT, not a linear integer: decode the 12-bit mantissa and 4-bit exponent before use (a consumer with no SFLOAT decoder must not render the raw uint16). The unit follows the same record's flags bit 0; the cuff is believed to report mmHg, and no kPa record from it has been observed. Zero or a special-value mantissa means "no result yet".

format.name: diastolic_sfloat
format.notes: Same SFLOAT encoding and unit rule as systolic_sfloat.

format.name: map_sfloat
format.notes: Mean arterial pressure, same SFLOAT encoding and unit rule. Always occupies offsets 5-6 but may decode to a special value on a record that carries systolic and diastolic.

characteristics.name: Blood Pressure Measurement
characteristics.notes:
The SIG Blood Pressure Measurement record, little-endian throughout, decoded exactly as the characteristic definition says and with no vendor quirk: flags byte, then systolic, diastolic and mean arterial pressure as three IEEE-11073 16-bit SFLOATs, then optional fields in flag order — 7-byte timestamp, SFLOAT pulse rate, uint8 user ID, uint16 measurement status. Minimum length 7 bytes. The format block below declares the fixed part; payload_formats.BloodPressureMeasurement walks the optional tail, whose offsets depend on the flags, and gives the SFLOAT rule and worked examples.
SFLOAT: the 16-bit value's low 12 bits are a two's-complement mantissa, the high 4 bits a two's-complement exponent, value = mantissa x 10^exponent. Mantissas 0x07ff (NaN), 0x0800 (NRes), 0x07fe (+INF), 0x0802 (-INF) and 0x0801 (reserved) are special and carry no value. The pressure unit follows flags bit 0: mmHg when clear, kPa when set (multiply by 7.500617 for mmHg).
The SIG profile specifies this characteristic as INDICATE; both open clients enable NOTIFY (the Android port writes CCCD 01 00) and receive records, so the cuff at least supports notifications. Records arrive while the cuff inflates and deflates, not only at the end: a client keeps the last record whose systolic and diastolic both decode finite and above zero with systolic greater than diastolic, debounces 1.5 s after the last notification, and treats a special-value systolic or diastolic as "no result". LibreArm additionally refuses to save a result outside systolic 40-260, diastolic 20-200, pulse 20-220.

cancel_measurement.description: Cancel a measurement in progress; the cuff stops inflating and releases pressure. LibreArm sends it on user cancel and on its 180 s watchdog, and warns that the cuff may not have stopped cleanly if the write fails.

start_measurement.description: Start a measurement: the cuff inflates, measures and deflates, streaming 0x2a35 records as it goes. Only send with the cuff fitted to a person who is ready for it (see safety_advisory). LibreArm checks battery first and abandons a run that yields no complete record within 180 s.

characteristics.name: QardioArm control
characteristics.notes: The vendor's one addition to the standard service: a two-byte command whose first byte is always f1. LibreArm writes with response when the characteristic advertises the write property and without response otherwise, and the Android port always writes with response, so the characteristic is known to accept write-with-response; which of the two properties the cuff actually declares has not been dumped. No reply or notification is documented on this characteristic — the response to a start is the stream of 0x2a35 records. A write that fails with a pairing-class ATT error means the bond is broken (see device.pairing).

services.name: Blood Pressure Service
services.notes: The Bluetooth SIG Blood Pressure Service, plus one vendor characteristic. The standard Blood Pressure Feature (0x2a49) and Intermediate Cuff Pressure (0x2a36) characteristics are not reported by either open client; whether the cuff exposes them is unknown. The measurement characteristic is secured: enabling its notifications is what triggers the bond.

characteristics.name: Battery Level
characteristics.notes: One byte, 0-100 percent; LibreArm discards anything above 100. Read on connect, before each measurement and after each result. The vendor manual says the app shows a low-battery symbol at about 25 percent and refuses to measure when the cells are depleted; LibreArm draws the lines at 20 percent (low) and 10 percent (blocks measurement). Four AAA alkaline cells; the manual says not to use rechargeables.

services.name: Battery Service
services.notes: Standard SIG Battery Service. LibreArm's README says "when the cuff exposes it" and the client tolerates its absence, so treat the service as optional until a GATT dump settles it; the Android port does not read it at all.
